title: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty
author: William George Jordan
public_title: Your willpower is a liar. Here is the proof.
hook: You believe your willpower stays full until you run out of it.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You believe your willpower stays full until you run out of it. William George Jordan wrote in 1911 that self-control is a majestic king. He thought you could rule every desire. Modern biology says he was wrong about the engine. Roy Baumeister at Florida State University found that willpower is not infinite. It is a muscle. His studies showed that using it for one task reduces it for the next. The result? You are not lazy. You are depleted. Jordan got the goal right. He missed the reality. Your brain does not have a limit set by character. It has a limit set by glucose. That is a chemical fact. Not a moral judgment. Later research confirmed this across different demographics. It is called ego depletion. So why do we assume we just need to try harder? Because we confuse effort with capacity. The fact is, capacity runs out. So next time you feel weak, remember your willpower is a battery. You believe your willpower stays full until you run out of it.

claims.claim: Willpower is a finite resource that depletes with use (ego depletion).
Self-control is described as a majestic, governing faculty.
